pr.title: fix(context): single body overrides other returns

summary: This PR changes c.body()'s TypeScript signature to return a properly typed Response with TypedResponse metadata (status/body type), fixing an issue where c.body() overrides the inferred status/type of other handler returns in a route with multiple return paths. The runtime behavior of #newResponse is unchanged; the change is primarily type-level plus a corresponding test update.

findings.rationale: body() now types its return as Response & TypedResponse<...>, but the underlying #newResponse implementation still returns a plain Response cast via 'as ReturnType<BodyRespond>'. If #newResponse's actual output ever diverges from the typed contract (e.g., different status handling), the type system won't catch it since it's force-cast.
findings.suggestedCheck: Confirm #newResponse always produces a Response consistent with the claimed TypedResponse<Data, Status, Format> contract for all overload branches (null data disallowed content, contentful headers etc.).

findings.rationale: Test change replaces reading c.res after multiple header sets with a second explicit c.body('Hi') call; behavior around header clearing when calling body twice is now implicitly relied upon and not obviously covered elsewhere.
findings.suggestedCheck: Verify calling c.body() multiple times still correctly reflects the latest header state used elsewhere in the codebase/tests.
